alignments.note: Connective rendered *Now*.
Substantival demonstrative expanded with a supplied generic noun; rule 17 keeps the head on the demonstrative, as `ταῦτα` → *these things* does.
Vocative noun, anarthrous, with no supplied address word (rule 89).

One Greek compound verb rendered by *have in a figure transferred*: both English elements gloss something, *transferred* answering to the `μετα-` element and *figure* to the `σχηματ-` core, so rule 66's compound clause heads on the core even though English syntax makes *transferred* the finite verb, exactly as `πιθανολογίᾳ` → *persuasiveness of speech* heads on *speech*. Heading on *transferred* as the lexical verb remains defensible and is the competing reading.
Preposition rendered *to*.
Reflexive pronoun.
Conjunction.
Name. SBLGNT.1CO.4.6.v002 is underdetermined between r00-base and r01, both of which write the name, so no textual question arises here (rule 12).
Proper preposition wrapped in the discontinuous frame *for … sakes*: rule 78 settles the head on the prepositional word, eleven corpus units to none.
Pronoun rendered by the possessive inside the *for … sakes* wrap.
Purpose conjunction realized by the word introducing its English clause (rule 40).
Preposition rendered *in*.
Pronoun.
Subjunctive with supplied subject and modal, headed on the lexical verb (rules 9 and 17).
Nominalizing article introducing the quoted maxim; English spells the construction with no word answering to the article itself (rules 23 and 61).
Ordinary negative rendered *not*; the following `εἷς` is not in this clause.

The Greek clause is verbless with a prepositional predicate, and the ASV supplies the italicized *to go*; rule 62 gives such a supplied lexical verb to the preposition, headed on the word realizing the preposition. Marking *to go* `added` is the competing reading, but rule 62's `τὰ παρ᾿ ὑμῶν` → *the things that came from you* is this same configuration.
Relative pronoun expanded with a supplied determiner and a **generic noun**; rule 77 gives the head to the nominal in that case, as JHN.8.26 and GAL.1.20 read *the things which*.
Perfect passive with its auxiliary, headed on the participle (rules 9 and 17). SBLGNT.1CO.4.6.v004 selected r00-base, which the projection carries.
Second purpose conjunction rendered *that*.
The ASV writes two English words, *no* and *one*, so the negator and the numeral split in the ordinary way under rule 2; rule 59's joining arm applies only where a single English word carries both.
Numeral rendered *one*.

Second-person plural verb: *of you* realizes the verb's own person and number and rides inside its unit under rule 9, discontinuously with *be puffed up* under rule 15. Marking *of you* `added` remains defensible, but no other source token licenses it and rule 9 lets an inflected verb take its English subject expression.
Preposition rendered *for*.
Article rendered *the* (rule 19).
Numeral rendered *one*.
Preposition rendered *against*.
Article rendered *the*.
Adjective rendered *other*.

review_notes: All 29 source and 46 target ids are partitioned exactly once.
The italicized *to go* is folded onto `ὑπέρ` under rule 62 rather than marked `added`; the competing reading is named in the unit's note.
The head of `μετεσχημάτισα` is taken on *figure* under rule 66's compound clause, with the competing head on *transferred* recorded.
